hook.text: Two patients with 'breast cancer' may have completely different genetic drivers. Same name, different diseases.

buildup.text: Cancer genomics sequences tumors to find the exact mutations driving growth. Then it matches them to targeted drugs.

discovery.text: HER2-positive breast cancer has a specific drug: Herceptin. Without HER2 testing, patients got chemo that didn't work.

twist.text: Tumors evolve resistance. A drug that works today may fail in months as cancer mutates around it. Genomics must keep up.

climax.text: Liquid biopsies detect tumor DNA in blood, tracking mutations in real time without surgery. A blood test beats a biopsy.

punchline.text: Cancer isn't one disease. Genomics treats each tumor as unique.

quiz.question: What does cancer genomics do?
options: Sequences tumors to match targeted drugs
